summary: Remote-controlled shell and filesystem access via WebSocket peer
details: When the agent starts, it connects to a configured WebSocket server and exposes a message router that gives the remote peer full administrative control over the installer's host. `terminal_create` messages call `handleTerminalCreate`, which spawns a system shell PTY (bash/PowerShell/cmd) inheriting the installer's environment; subsequent `terminal_input` frames are written directly into that PTY, yielding arbitrary command execution. The same router handles `read_file`, `write_file`, `list_directory`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, `git_commit`, `git_push`, `file_search`, and a `proxy_request`/`proxy_ws_*` path — arbitrary filesystem read/write and git repository mutation from the network. A `upgrade_agent` message causes the process to spawn a detached script that runs `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and restart via systemd/launchd/PM2, letting the same remote party control which future versions are installed and executed. Whoever controls the configured server has full remote code execution and workspace administration on any host running this agent.
